newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Belgian deputy PM in Vietnam for port deal.
newsitem.headline: Belgian deputy PM in Vietnam for port deal.

text.p: Belgium's Deputy Prime Minister is due to arrive in Vietnam on Saturday for a visit timed to coincide with the signing ceremony for construction of a huge industrial zone at the northern port of Haiphong.

The Belgian Embassy in Hanoi said in a statement on Thursday that Philippe Maystadt, also minister of finance and trade, would meet Deputy Prime Minister Tran Duc Luong and Communist Party Secretary General Do Muoi during his visit.
He will also travel to Haiphong, where a consortium including Belgium's International Port Engineering and Management (IPEM) is due to sign a joint venture agreement.
The other partners in the project to build an industrial park on the Dinh Vu peninsula are U.S. insurer American International Group and Thailand's Asian Infrastructure Development Co.
The daily Vietnam News said in a report that the venture would involve investment funds of up to $556 million.

The park is part of a larger project that includes a deep-sea port, whose terminals in the Red River delta will be able to accomodate fully laden 10,000-tonne vessels, in the early stages of development.
Ultimately, they will take 30,000-tonne ships and have a handling capacity of at least 12 million tonnes a year.
Vietnam hopes the new port facility will make Haiphong a major shipping hub for East and Southeast Asia.
Belgium established diplomatic relations with Hanoi in 1973, the year an accord was signed in Paris to restore peace to Vietnam.

In 1993, Belgium pledged 450 million Belgian francs ($14 million) in direct aid to Vietnam over three years and in 1994 and 1995 granted two development cooperation soft loans totalling 300 million francs ($9.3 million).
Belgium now ranks 31st among foreign investors in Vietnam, with total commitments of $27 million for eight projects.

Maystadt is to leave Hanoi for Singapore next Wednesday and Secretary of State for Development Cooperation Reginald Moreels, who will accompany him on the visit to Vietnam, is due to leave for Laos on the same day.
